story: Osiris, god of fertility, agriculture, and the afterlife, was the eldest son of the earth god and the sky goddess, and was both brother and husband to Isis. His brother Set desired his throne and conspired with the Queen of Ethiopia and seventy-two accomplices to kill him. Set tricked Osiris into entering a box, sealed it with lead, and threw it into the Nile. Isis searched for her husband and found him embedded in a tamarisk tree trunk that was holding up the roof of a palace in Byblos on the Phoenician coast. She retrieved the body, but Set found it again and cut it into pieces, scattering them. Isis, joined by her sister Nephthys, searched the land and recovered all the pieces except Osiris's genitals. Isis reassembled and wrapped the body, then used magic to briefly revive him so she could conceive a child. She later gave birth to their son, Horus, who eventually avenged his father by defeating Set. In another telling, Osiris was an ancient king who taught his people to abandon cannibalism and travelled the world with his sons, a nature spirit, woodland spirits, and nine goddesses of inspiration, teaching humanity to cultivate the vine and sow wheat and barley. After returning home, he was murdered by his evil brother, who divided his body into twenty-six pieces and distributed them among fellow conspirators to implicate them. Isis and the strong hero (Horus) avenged him and slew the murderer. Isis recovered all the parts except the phallus, secretly buried them, and made replicas that were distributed to various locations, which became centers of Osiris's worship. Thereafter, Osiris ruled as lord of the dead and the underworld.
